title: Immigration Roundup: India's EB-3 Date Advances, New Zealand Widens Business Visas
excerpt: The November 2026 Visa Bulletin moves India's EB-3 final action date three weeks while EB-2 stays frozen at November 2013, and New Zealand broadens business visitor and specialist work pathways effective October 20.
body:
• India's EB-3 final action date advances three weeks to January 22, 2014 in the November 2026 Visa Bulletin; EB-2 India stays at November 1, 2013 and EB-1 India stays at February 1, 2023.
  • Reader action: USCIS will accept employment-based I-485 filings in November using the Dates for Filing chart — for EB-2 and EB-3 India that cutoff is January 15, 2015, so if your priority date is earlier than that date, you can file in November even though final approval still waits for the final action date.
  • Worldwide EB-2 advances three months to April 1, 2025 and worldwide EB-3 advances one month to June 15, 2024, widening the gap with India's frozen dates.
  • New Zealand, effective October 20, 2026, expanded permitted Business Visitor Visa activities and clarified Specific Purpose Work Visa routes for contractual service suppliers and independent professionals.

The U.S. Department of State's November 2026 Visa Bulletin brings modest movement for employment-based green card applicants, with India's most-watched categories largely holding still. According to the November 2026 Visa Bulletin published by the Department of State, the EB-3 final action date for India advances three weeks, from January 1, 2014 to January 22, 2014. EB-2 India remains unchanged at November 1, 2013, and EB-1 India remains at February 1, 2023. The Murthy Law Firm's summary of the bulletin reports the same dates.

Where the November Dates Stand for India

For applicants chargeable to India, the final action dates — the dates that govern when a green card can actually be approved — are February 1, 2023 for EB-1, November 1, 2013 for EB-2, and January 22, 2014 for EB-3, including EB-3 Other Workers. EB-5 Unreserved for India remains at December 1, 2023, while all three EB-5 set-aside categories — rural, high unemployment and infrastructure — remain current for every country, according to the bulletin. Outside India, the picture moved faster: EB-1 for China advances one month to August 1, 2023, EB-2 for most other countries advances three months to April 1, 2025, and EB-3 for most other countries advances one month to June 15, 2024. China EB-3 also advances two weeks to January 22, 2022.

The Filing Window That Matters in November

The practical opportunity sits in the second chart. WR Immigration's digest reports that USCIS will allow employment-based adjustment of status applicants to use the Dates for Filing chart in November. On that chart, the India cutoff is July 1, 2024 for EB-1 and January 15, 2015 for both EB-2 and EB-3, according to the State Department bulletin. An applicant whose priority date is earlier than the applicable Dates for Filing cutoff may file Form I-485 in November, provided they otherwise meet adjustment eligibility requirements. Filing does not approve the green card — final approval remains subject to visa availability under the Final Action Dates chart — but a filed I-485 is the step that typically opens the path to employment and travel authorization while the case waits. Applicants should confirm the chart designation for the month they file on the USCIS adjustment of status filing charts page before submitting.

New Zealand Widens Business and Specialist Pathways

The same digest reports a second change relevant to Indian professionals. Effective October 20, 2026, New Zealand broadened permitted activities under its Business Visitor Visa and clarified eligibility under the Specific Purpose Work Visa. Immigration New Zealand's guidance lists the expanded business visitor activities: attending informal training limited to observation and theoretical instruction that does not lead to a formal qualification, conducting business transactions on behalf of a business in New Zealand in qualifying management or financial services roles, and participating in tourism conventions as a travel agent, tour guide or tour operator. The Specific Purpose framework now also recognizes contractual service suppliers and independent professionals delivering service contracts or specialized assignments, subject to qualification, experience and documentation requirements, and in some cases labour market testing. Other work activities, or a business stay longer than three months, still require a work visa.

What Has Not Changed

The digest also noted that the Labor Department's PERM reform proposal has completed federal review. That development is not new to Videshi readers — we covered the White House clearance and what the overhaul could mean for employer-sponsored green cards in our earlier report, White House Clears Labor Department Plan to Overhaul PERM Green Card Rules. Existing PERM recruitment requirements remain unchanged until the department publishes a proposed rule in the Federal Register and completes a public comment period.

What to Watch Next

Compare priority dates against both November charts now, because filing eligibility can change monthly. The December bulletin will show whether India's EB-2 date moves at all in fiscal year 2027, and the PERM proposal's Federal Register publication will set the comment clock for the first major rewrite of PERM rules since 2004.
